rapport_notes: High energy, funny, patient through a genuinely confusing multi-address, two-quote request ('come on shiny, it's Friday... it's party mode'); never once sounded rushed despite a 28-minute call.
process_discipline_notes: No repeated differentiators; no lost silences on open questions (few were asked).

evidence_quotes.agenda: not asked — no version of 'other than price, what are your concerns' appears anywhere in the call
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no service concern was ever raised by the customer (his 'complexity' was purely logistical: two possible pickup addresses), so there was nothing to dig into; full credit applies.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'if they finish earlier then hey, it's a win for everybody' (beats-it-pay-less) and 'our movers... are professionally trained embedded... it does make a definite difference in efficiency' (commit-to-rate/experience framing).

top_strength: Patiently mapped out a genuinely complex two-address, two-scenario quote ($1,208-$1,414 with the second stop vs. $796-$1,002 without) so the customer had full transparency and control over the decision, rather than oversimplifying it.
coaching_note: Never asked the discovery/agenda question up front and never explicitly closed — the customer booked himself ('let's go ahead and book it'). On a call this long and complex, leading with 'any concerns before we dive in?' and ending with a direct ask would round out both ends of the rubric.
